cbt.needBothFields: Fill in at least the situation and the thought
cbt.historyEmpty: Nothing here yet. The first record is the most useful one.
cbt.aiSystem:
You are a careful cognitive behavioural therapy assistant inside the GeQu app. The user has ADHD.

You are given a completed thought-record entry: situation, automatic thought, emotion, evidence for and against, alternative thought.

Do three things, briefly:
1. Name the cognitive distortions visible in the automatic thought (from this list: all-or-nothing thinking, catastrophizing, should statements, mind reading, mental filter, labeling, overgeneralization, emotional reasoning, personalization, discounting the positive). Only the ones that are actually there.
2. Ask 1–2 questions that would help look at the situation more accurately.
3. Suggest one more balanced version of the thought — not "everything's fine", but more honest and precise.

Write in English, warmly, in the second person, and without moralising. Format as short Markdown with subheadings. Rely only on what is written in the entry.

schulte.label: Schulte table
limitations: Speed depends on screen size and on whether you tap or click.
Repeat attempts back to back are usually faster from familiarity with the grid, not from attention.

reaction.label: Reaction speed
limitations: Screen and input latency are part of the result — numbers are not comparable across devices.
This measures simple reaction, not attention in general.

tmt.label: Number connection
limitations: This is not the clinical Trail Making Test: the protocol and the norms are different.
A small screen slows hitting the targets noticeably.

stroop.label: Stroop test
limitations: This counts correct answers against the clock, not the classic interference score.
The result depends heavily on how much you rush.

digitspan.label: Digit span
limitations: Saying the digits aloud or writing them down changes the result sharply.
One attempt is a rough estimate: the spread between attempts is usually about one level.

corsi.label: Corsi blocks
limitations: Visuo-spatial memory, not memory in general.
The size and layout of the grid affect the result.

nback.label: N-Back
limitations: Accuracy depends on the N you chose — only compare the same level.
Training N-back improves N-back; transfer to other tasks is not established.

gonogo.label: Go / No-Go
limitations: One number mixes speed and restraint — they are worth looking at separately.
A short run gives a wide spread.

arithmetic.label: Mental arithmetic
limitations: Depends on how practised you are at mental arithmetic as much as on your current state.

switching.label: Task switching
limitations: The switch cost is not measured separately here — only the total score.

attempt.heading: How to read this
attempt.noAttempts: No attempts yet. The first result becomes your reference point — there is nothing to compare it with, and that is fine.
attempt.tooFew: You have {{count}} of the {{needed}} attempts needed for a comparison. Below that, a single result says almost nothing — the spread between attempts is usually larger than the difference between a good day and a bad one.
attempt.selfOnly: The comparison is always only against your own attempts. This is not a normed test — the result is not compared with anyone else.

regulate.title: Regulation
regulate.hint: No score — this is not a test

arithmetic.blurb: Count in your head as fast as you can. A mistake costs 1 point.

breathing.heading: Box breathing (4-4-4-4)
breathing.blurb: Follow your breath around the sides of the square: in, hold, out, hold. Cycle: {{done}}/{{total}}

corsi.blurb: Remember the order of the flashes and repeat it by tapping the squares.

digitSpan.wrong: Not quite. It was: {{correct}}. Back to 3.
digitSpan.blurb: Remember the sequence of digits and enter it in the right order.

goNoGo.blurb: Click only on the <1>green</1> circle. On <3>red</3> — do not press anything.

nBack.blurb: Working-memory accuracy. The result is saved.
nBack.heading: N-Back training
nBack.intro: Squares will appear on the screen. Press the button if a square appears in the same position as <1>N steps ago</1>.

reaction.blurb: Wait for green, then click as fast as you can.
reaction.area: Reaction area — press when it turns green

schulte.blurb: Look at the centre. Find the numbers in order.

stroop.blurb: Press the COLOUR of the word, not what it says.

switching.blurb: The rule changes as you go — watch the prompt at the top.

trail.blurb: Click in order: 1 → A → 2 → B → 3 and so on.
